AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DTD:31-08-2010 PASSED IN MVC NO.1457/2007 ON THE FILE OF THE MEMBER, MAC T-IX, BELLARY, AWARDING THE COMPENSATION OF RS.94,400/- WITH INTEREST AT THE RATE OF 6% P.A., FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL ITS DEPOSIT.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

Challenging judgment and award dated 31.08.2010 passed by Motor Accident Tribunal IX, Bellary,
in MVC No.1457/2007, this appeal is filed by insurer.
2. Brief facts as stated are that on 19.08.2007, claimant - Mohan Shanbag was riding motorcycle bearing registration no.KA-02/EZ-7811 on Challekere road along with Manjunath Reddy as pillion.
Motorcycle turned turtle on account of rash and negligent riding by its rider.
As a result, both rider and pillion rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Despite taking treatment, they sustained physical disability.

3. Claiming compensation, they filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
against owner and insurer of motorcycle.
4. On service of notice and on contest, claim petition was opposed on ground of negligence, liability as well quantum.
5. Tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence of claimants as PW1 and PW2 and got marked Exhibits P1 to P19.

Official of insurer was examined as RW1 and got marked Insurance policy as Ex.R1.
6.

On consideration, tribunal held that accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of motorcycle by its rider and as he had valid and effective driving licence and motorcycle was covered under insurance policy, it held insurer liable to pay compensation of Rs.94,400/-.
Aggrieved by award insofar as finding on negligence, insurer is in appeal.

sentences.text: 7. Smt. Anusha, Advocate for Sri. S.K.Kayakamath, learned counsel for insurer submitted that Ex.P5-charge sheet was filed against rider - claimant herein and therefore, fastening of liability upon insurer when claimant himself was rash and negligent was not justified.

8. On the other hand, Sri S.B.Doddagoudar advocate, on behalf of Sri Chandrashekar Chakalabli,
learned counsel for respondent no.1 sought to support award.
9. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award and record.
10.
This is insurer's appeal challenging on finding regarding negligence.
Claimants have not preferred appeal.

Therefore, point that arise for consideration is:
"Whether finding of tribunal on liability against insurer was justified?"
11.

In support of contention that claimant himself was rash and negligent, insurer is relying upon charge sheet - Ex.P5.
12.
On perusal of award wherein there is detailed examination of records.

It is noted from Ex.P2 - spot panchanama that accident took place on State highway no.19, wherein width of road was 25ft.
and it was running north to south.
It was also noted that motorcycle had fallen down on left side of road.
Tribunal has noted from records that road was newly formed and seems to be one of probable cause for accident.
In cross-examination of PW.1 except eliciting that rider was riding it in high speed, there are no suggestions or elicitations with regard to reason for accident.
There is no specific suggestion about speed at which vehicle was being ridden.
Though admission about filing of charge sheet is elicited, same would not amount to admission of reason for accident, especially, when there is observation about newly laid road.
Under circumstances, I do not see any good or sufficient grounds to interfere with finding of tribunal.
13. Therefore, point for consideration is answered in negative.

Consequently, following:
ORDER a. Appeal is dismissed.
b. Amount in deposit is ordered to be transmitted to Tribunal for payment.
